items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Edmund I got to know very well.

ctx.x: Edmund I got to know very well. He led the house band there for a long time. Of course he was a bridge from New Orleans. He grew up in a town near there. He was part of the New Orleans scene. He also – he reminds me of this time with Louis Armstrong. He was with the All Stars for a while. He said something to me. They often played the same repertory almost night after night after night. I didn’t quite have the nerve to say, doesn’t it get boring? But when he said to me – I forget the context – he said, “I still…

Let’s talk about that for a moment. Those of us that never heard Armstrong in person, we may listen to the West End Blues or all this kind of stuff. But from what I understand and from what you just alluded to – not alluded, but what you just said – that there was something in his sound – there was something there – like you heard him at Symphony Hall – that of course could never be captured on a record, like there is I guess about every artist. How would you direct us towards that indefinable thing that has been…

items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1958-07-18
items.q: I met him through, through, you may know Nat Hentoff? Oh, yes. Well, Nat Hentoff was a disc jockey in Boston. So he said it's a guy used to be in the army and he's a psychiatrist. So he'd like to see you. You know, he'd like to meet you. So I was in Boston, so he took me up to this guy's house.

ctx.x: Pretty long though. Huh? You still have pretty long fingers. Yeah, and I don't know why they're blunt like that.

That's the big end there. Yeah, a psychiatrist, maybe, I shouldn't tell you this, but a psychiatrist, he saw me, he wanted to meet me. I didn't know him. I met him through, through, you may know Nat Hentoff? Oh, yes. Well, Nat Hentoff was a disc jockey in Boston. So he said it's a guy used to be in the army and he's a psychiatrist. So he'd like to see you. You know, he'd like to meet you. So I was in Boston, so he took me up to this guy's house. He said, I didn't know who he was. So he said he was, used to be a…
Sounds like punching filling, almost like you're reading your palm. Yeah, yeah.
